paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.

annotations.annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the "Number of child nodes (Tree Width)", and the accuracy at a specified level for two different models, "GPT-4o" and "Claude-3.5-Sonnet". The x-axis is labeled "Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)" and follows a linear scale with values ranging from 1 to 7, marked at intervals of 2. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy@1 (%)" and also uses a linear scale, spanning from 15% to 35%, with tick marks at 5% intervals. The plot includes two lines; the first line represents "GPT-4o" and is shown in a blue color with circular markers and a solid line style. Starting at an accuracy of 24.4% at a tree width of 1, it increases to 28.9% at width 3, peaks at 34.4% at width 5, and then declines to 31.1% at width 7. The second line represents "Claude-3.5-Sonnet" and is depicted in the same shade of blue with 'x' shaped markers and a dotted line style. It starts at an accuracy of 26.7% at width 1, increases to 27.8% at width 3, reaches a peak of 24.4% at width 5, and ends at a lower value of 20.0% at width 7. Both lines intersect at an x-value of around 2 and follow an increasing then decreasing trend with increasing x-value. There is a legend box on the top of the plot to identify the lines of "GPT-4o" and "Claude-3.5-Sonnet".
